systems.name: Body & shell
systems.description: The 911 body keeps its unbroken roofline from windshield to tail. The Turbo adds flared rear arches for wider tyres and the signature 'whale tail' spoiler.
systems.principle: A welded steel unibody carries the loads; two rows of seats sit ahead of an engine hung behind the rear axle. In the source model the painted shell is one continuous mesh, so doors and lids do not separate.

systems.name: Glass & lights
systems.description: A curved windshield, side glass and a small rear window; the round headlights on the front fenders are the 911's identifying feature.
systems.principle: Glass is set in rubber seals in the classic way. Round halogen headlights sit high on the fenders; indicators and tail lights run horizontally.

systems.name: Cockpit
systems.description: A 2+2 cockpit with five round dials, a three-spoke wheel and sport seats. The source model has a simplified interior.
systems.principle: The classic 911 layout: rev counter in the centre, ignition key to the left of the wheel in the Le Mans tradition, and a long gear lever reaching the rear-mounted gearbox.

systems.name: Turbocharged flat-six
systems.description: A 3.0-litre air-cooled flat-six mounted behind the rear axle. A single KKK turbocharger earned the car the 'Turbo' badge.
systems.principle: A large centrifugal fan blows air over finned cylinders instead of a radiator. Exhaust gas spins the turbine, which compresses the intake charge; the famous lag-then-surge is the 930's character.

systems.name: Gearbox & rear axle
systems.description: A four-speed manual gearbox sits just ahead of the engine and drives the rear wheels through half-shafts.
systems.principle: Engine behind, gearbox in front of it: a compact transaxle package. Rear weight bias gives traction under power but demands skill at the limit.

systems.name: Fuel tank
systems.description: An 80-litre tank sits in the nose under the luggage floor, balancing the rear-mounted engine.
systems.principle: Rear-engined cars put the tank at the front to even out weight distribution. Fuel is pumped the length of the car to the engine.

systems.name: Torsion-bar suspension
systems.description: MacPherson struts with longitudinal torsion bars at the front, semi-trailing arms with transverse torsion bars at the rear. No coil springs as on modern cars.
systems.principle: A torsion bar is a steel rod that twists instead of a spring that compresses, saving space and weight. Separate dampers control the motion. The Turbo has bigger anti-roll bars and wide rear tyres to handle the power.

systems.name: Wheels & brakes
systems.description: Forged Fuchs 'cloverleaf' 16-inch alloys with wider tyres at the rear. Ventilated disc brakes on all four wheels.
systems.principle: Wider rear tyres carry the extra load and traction of the rear engine and drive. Forged wheels are lighter than cast ones, reducing unsprung mass.

pieces.body.shell: In the source model the whole painted shell, doors, hood, fenders and engine lid, is one continuous mesh. On the real car these are separate welded panels and hinged lids.

notes: Figures for the 930 Turbo 3.0 (1975–1977). The artist lists Pirelli P7 tyres and 16-inch Fuchs wheels, a later fitment.
